location: Thm informal:frz (iv), third bullet (line 353); also the claim "all $93$ sub-supports agree with the stated conditions" (line 358; app-informal.tex line 235)
problem: For supports containing both ZR and V, the theorem states only the full-support rule and one POS example. Yet V2 "checks" this family against an unstated rule, and only for w(ZR) > w(V): SEP if the support avoids UNI, PAIR, EMP, else Z. SEP is selected, for example, for {INT, ZR, V}, which the theorem never mentions.
proposed_fix: Replace the third bullet with: "support $\mathrm{DC}\cup\{\mathrm{ZR},\mathrm V\}$: Z iff $w(\mathrm{ZR})>w(\mathrm V)$, ties to STRAT. For $\{\mathrm{ZR},\mathrm V\}\subseteq$ support $\subseteq\mathrm{DC}\cup\{\mathrm{ZR},\mathrm V\}$: if $w(\mathrm{ZR})>w(\mathrm V)$, SEP if the support avoids UNI, PAIR, EMP, else Z; if $w(\mathrm V)>w(\mathrm{ZR})$, POS if it avoids DIFF, EMP, else STRAT (e.g.\ $\{\mathrm{INT},\mathrm{UNI},\mathrm{PAIR},\mathrm{ZR},\mathrm V\}$ gives POS); if $w(\mathrm{ZR})=w(\mathrm V)$, POS if it avoids DIFF, EMP, else SEP if it avoids UNI, PAIR, EMP, else STRAT." I verified this rule against comprehension_toy.learner on 160 cases (32 sub-supports × 5 weight patterns) with 0 mismatches.

location: Thm informal:robust (d2), line 390: "expansion or a library lemma removes them"
problem: Prop expansion is about a single target and needs step-expressiveness. In the vague case an expansion must be one chain of steps that are g-short under every sharpening at once, and such a chain may not exist (round-2 flag). The appendix already says "when one exists".
proposed_fix: Replace with "adding the step as a library lemma to every $R_\sigma$ removes them, and so does an expansion into steps of $\Stg{g}{\mathrm{SV}}$ when one exists".

location: Prop informal:emergence (c), line 423: "but a uniform template would yield a $\PA$-proof of $\Con(\PA)$"
problem: Uniform derivability depends on the calculus. The Gödel-II argument needs rules closed under substituting a fresh variable for the numeral letter, as in a standard Hilbert calculus; the appendix says so. A complete calculus whose decidable library contains ⊢θ(n̄) for every n makes the schema uniformly 1-step derivable (round-2 flag).
proposed_fix: Replace with "fails in general: in a standard Hilbert calculus for $\PA$ (rules closed under substituting a fresh variable for a numeral), ``infer $\theta(\bar n)$'' with $\theta(n)=$ ``$n$ codes no $\PA$-proof of $0=1$'' has all instances provable, but a uniform template would yield a $\PA$-proof of $\Con(\PA)$; uniform derivability is relative to the calculus and its library".

location: line 416: "its use for the sorites over precisifications is Edgington's \citep{edgington1997vagueness}"
problem: Edgington applies the Adams-style bound to verities (degrees of closeness to clear truth). She mentions the Lewis–Kamp measure-over-precisifications reading without committing to it, so 'over precisifications' is not her view.
proposed_fix: Replace with: "its use for the sorites is Edgington's, with her verities in place of a measure over precisifications \citep{edgington1997vagueness}".
